Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Riley Jennings  
Member ID: W995720068  
Reference number: POC-39DE00339B-16726  
Requested service: Knee arthroscopy with meniscus surgery  
CPT: 29881  
Notice date: August 19, 2026

Dear UPMC Health Plan Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

The submitted clinical records document a persistent, objectively confirmed, functionally significant knee condition that has not improved with appropriate conservative treatment. The records support the medical necessity of the requested arthroscopic meniscus surgery for the following reasons:

- I have had nine months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy over 10 weeks, from May 8, 2026, through July 17, 2026. Therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, and the physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 13, 2026, provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on July 18, 2026, showed a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. The MRI also showed preserved articular cartilage and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes.
- I have mechanical symptoms, including locking and giving way. I cannot squat or kneel and am limited to level walking.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- The records do not identify active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

These records address the duration and severity of symptoms, failure of conservative treatment, objective imaging findings, physical examination findings, mechanical symptoms, and functional impairment. They also document the absence of the specific medical factors identified in the submitted records that could interfere with treatment.

If UPMC Health Plan believes that any particular information remains necessary, please identify each missing item specifically and explain how it is required for review of CPT 29881. Please do not treat the submission as simply incomplete without identifying the missing documentation. I request that UPMC Health Plan provide the exact clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including the applicable InterQual Connect criteria or other criteria used for CPT 29881, together with the relevant version or effective date. The public UPMC materials I located do not disclose the actual medical-necessity criteria for this request.

I request that UPMC Health Plan reconsider the denial and approve the requested knee arthroscopy with meniscus surgery. If the denial is upheld, please provide the complete clinical rationale, the specific criteria applied, the records considered, and the instructions for any further appeal or external review.

Please associate this appeal with reference number POC-39DE00339B-16726. The appeal deadline stated in the notice is February 15, 2027.

Enclosures:

1. Adverse benefit determination dated August 19, 2026  
2. MRI report dated July 18, 2026  
3. Physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 visits from May 8, 2026, through July 17, 2026  
4. Medication and injection treatment history  
5. Orthopedic examination and clinical assessment  
6. Any additional records submitted with the original prior authorization request

Sincerely,

Riley Jennings
